questions.question: Consider AD is a tangent to a circle of radius 6 cm. AC is a secant meeting the circle at B and CD is a diameter. If AB is 7 cm, then the value of AC (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 6 cm

AB = 7 cm

CD = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

**Formula used:**

AD² = AC × AB

AC² - CD² = AD²

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b186b8aac889f8998a954c1157c7da19637a4433557a57e81575aa4777b0ba34.png] 

Substituting the values in the Tangent-Secant Theorem:

AC² - 12² = AC × 7

⇒ AC² - 144 = 7AC

⇒ AC² - 7AC - 144 = 0

This is a quadratic equation, solving using the quadratic formula:

⇒ AC2 - 16AC + 9AC - 144 = 0

⇒ AC(AC - 16) + 9(AC - 16) = 0

⇒ (AC - 16)(AC + 9) = 0

⇒ AC = 16 or AC = -9

⇒ AC = 16 cm (since length cannot be negative)

**∴ The value of AC is 16 cm.**

questions.question: A and S are two points on a circle with centre O. AT is a tangent, such that ∠SAT = 45°. N is a point on OA, such that SN = 10 cm. The length of the median OM of ΔSON is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠SAT = 45° 

SN = 10 cm

**Concept used:**

**1.** The length of the median drawn from the vertex of the right angle is half the length of the triangle's hypotenuse.

**2.** The angle between the tangent and the line joining the center of a circle and the point of contact of the tangent to the circle is equal to 90°.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e4b5a9cdc1ca30f925ae986f84cbd2bb17970c13e7c1845a81cb860bd3ccf98.png] 

As AT is the tangent,

∠OAT = 90°

Again ∠SAT = 45°

∴ ∠OAS = 90° - 45° = 45°

In ΔOAS,

OA = OS = Radius

∠OAS = ∠OSA = 45°

Then ∠NOS = 180° - 45° - 45° = 90°

⇒ ΔSON is a right-angles triangle

Thus, OM = SN/2

⇒ OM = 10/2 = 5 cm

**∴ The length of the median OM of ΔSON is 5 cm.**

questions.question: Two circles with centres M and N have radii 5 cm and 8 cm, respectively. The circles touch each other externally at point T. A line PR is drawn such that the points M, T and N lie on PR, P being closer to M. From P, a tangent PQ = 12 cm is drawn to the circle with centre M touching at Q, and from R, another tangent RS = 15 cm is drawn to the circle with centre N touching at S. What is the length (in cm) of PR?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the circle with center M = 5 cm

Radius of the circle with center N = 8 cm

Tangent PQ = 12 cm

Tangent RS = 15 cm

The circles touch externally at point T.

**Formula used:**

Use the Pythagorean theorem to find PM and NR:

PM² = PQ² + MQ²

NR² = RS² + NS²

Total length of PR = PM + MN + NR

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b8c7ec3d7d2e733308f48491acaeab6cf42f4738ef0dfb91e5b8ae5cdcbbf79.png] 

For PM:

PM² = 12² + 5²

⇒ PM² = 144 + 25

⇒ PM² = 169

⇒ PM = √169 = 13 cm

For NR:

NR² = 15² + 8²

⇒ NR² = 225 + 64

⇒ NR² = 289

⇒ NR = √289 = 17 cm

Now, distance between M and N:

MN = 5 cm + 8 cm = 13 cm

Total length of PR:

PR = PM + MN + NR

⇒ PR = 13 cm + 13 cm + 17 cm = 43 cm

**∴ The length of PR is 43 cm.**

questions.question: A rectangle ABCD is inscribed in a circle with centre O. Its diagonal CA is produced to a point E, outside the circle. ED is a tangent to the circle at D. If AC = 2BC, then what is the measure of ∠DEC?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd836491905842cda445a1701d23a0d88f85fc201a3dfc43d0b2a7c56c81b602.png] 

As the diagonals of the rectangle are equal and bisect each other,

AO = OC = DO = OB = ½ AC = ½ BD

Given:

AC = 2BC

⇒ AO = OC = BO = BC

In ΔOCB, OC = OB = BC

⇒ ΔOCB is an equilateral triangle

⇒ ∠COB = 60°

⇒ ∠DOA = 60° (∵ Vertically opposite angle)

In ΔODE, ∠ODE = 90° (∵ Angle made by a tangent and the radius is 90°)

In ΔODE, sum of the angles = 180°

(∵ ∠DOE = ∠DOA)

⇒ ∠DEC = 180 - ∠ODE - ∠DOE 

⇒ ∠DEC = 180 – 90° - 60°

⇒ ∠DEC = 30°

questions.question: R wishes to use a stick of length 6 units as common internal tangent to two circles of radius two units and three units. What can be the maximum distance (in units) between the centres of the circle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of common internal tangent (L) = 6 units

Radius of the first circle (r₁) = 2 units

Radius of the second circle (r₂) = 3 units

**Formula used:**

For two circles with radii r₁ and r₂, and the length of the common internal tangent L, the distance d between their centers can be given by:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6832f9ac1095b2c2012cea50525f30a52ea4ebb68b8a419057700b7c4fe13d78.png] 

sqrt{d² - (r₁ + r₂)²} = L

**Calculation:**

sqrt{d² - (2 + 3)²} = 6

⇒ sqrt{d² - 25} = 6

⇒ sqrt{d² - 25} = 6

⇒ (d² - 25) = 6²

⇒ (d² - 25) = 36

⇒ d² = 36 + 25

⇒ d = sqrt{61}

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Two circles touch each other internally. Their radii are 3 cm and 4 cm. What is the length of the biggest chord of the circle with radii 4 cm which is outside the inner circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two circles touch each other internally.

The radius of the inner circle = 3 cm

The radius of the outer circle = 4 cm

**Concept used:**

When two circles are touch each other internally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png] 

When the largest chord of bigger circle is tangent to the inner circle (smaller circle).

Then, 

Radius of inner circle (PD) = x cm

Radius of bigger circle (OB) = y cm

OP = Distance between two centers = Radius of bigger circle - radius of inner circle

⇒OP = y - x

CD = Diameter of inner circle = 2 × (radius of inner circle)

⇒ CD = 2x

OC = Difference between chord and bigger circle centre = CD - PD - OP

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 2x - x - (y - x) = 2x - y

Calculation:

Let the biggest chord of the circle with radii 4 cm which is outside the inner circle = AB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png] 

From the figure, we know that

PD = 3 cm 

OD = 4 cm

OP = OD - PD

⇒ OP = 4 - 3 = 1 cm

⇒ CD = 2 x PD = 2 x 3 = 6 cm

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 6 - 3 - 1 = 2 cm

⇒ OB = 4 cm = radius of outer circle

By using Pythagoras theorem, we can write that

OB2 = BC2 + OC2

⇒ 42 = BC2 + 22

⇒ BC2 = 16 - 4

⇒ BC2 = 12

⇒ BC = sqrt{12} = 2sqrt{3} cm

Now, 

The length of biggest chord AB = 2 x BC = 2 x 2sqrt{3} = 4sqrt{3} cm

**∴ The length of the biggest chord of the circle outside the inner circle is 4sqrt{3} cm.**
